payload.headline: Apple steady at 352.45; price still above every value estimate as estimates slip

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong, cash-rich business. At 352.45, though, the price assumes free cash flow grows about 27.5% a year, while analysts are cutting their profit estimates.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait for a clean breakout or a pullback that holds support.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at 300.56, add at 264.78; swing entry only on a close above 356.07

payload.happening: Apple closed at 352.45, up 0.15% on the day. That is just above a support zone at 347.89–351.46 and below resistance at 354.15–356.07. The only news is a reported iFixit teardown saying the HomeView device will be difficult to repair, plus a speculative CNBC piece on Apple as a 'safe haven'. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-28.
payload.business: Some of today's facts change the business itself. Inventory is up 154% from a year earlier, while latest-quarter sales are up 12%. Unsold product can force price cuts and squeeze margins. Growth is also slowing. Quarterly sales grew 11.72% from a year earlier, down from 16.6% two quarters ago. Analysts have cut next-quarter profit-per-share estimates by 3.8% over 30 days. The cash engine is not at risk today. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) is 136.1B over the last year, a 28.41% margin. The operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%. Debt exceeds cash by 23.4B, but liquidity of 56.7B covers near-term needs. Other items change sentiment or governance, not demand or margins. These include the reported teardown, the CNBC opinion piece, and a new investigation risk in the latest annual report. That investigation risk is a governance flag that matters only if it grows. Segment data is not available, so it is unclear which product lines are driving the inventory build.

worth.text: Every valuation method lands below the price. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash, using a 10.1% discount rate) gives 141.1 in the bear case, 195.38 in the base case and 255.28 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. To justify 352.45, free cash flow would need to start growing about 27.5% a year. Sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years. The starting-growth assumption drives the gap. At 20% starting growth the value is 264.78, and at 30% it is 387.1. Multiples tell the same story. The price is 39.2 times trailing earnings and 33.2 times next year's estimate. It is 10.7 times sales, against a peer median of 5.4, and sits at the 98th percentile of its own 5-year range. Margins also matter. If the operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 198.18.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free-cash-flow growth: the price needs about 27.5% a year, while sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 136.1B over the last year, from 98.8B a year earlier.
The operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%, so each dollar of sales is turning into more profit.
The share count fell 1.56% in a year, so each remaining share owns a bigger slice of the business.
bear: The price implies 27.5% starting free-cash-flow growth, far above last year's 15% sales growth.
Inventory is up 154% while sales are up 12%, which can lead to discounting and lower margins.
Analysts cut next-quarter profit-per-share estimates by 3.8% in 30 days, and the stock trades at 10.7 times sales against a peer median of 5.4.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole fair-value range, so it is too high to buy.
The top of Apple's own price-to-sales history and of my range, close to the rising 200-day average of 302.08. Buying starts to make sense at or below this level.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still above recent sales growth. Adding is justified at this price.

longterm.why: The business is high quality and generates a lot of cash, but the price needs far more growth than the company is delivering, and estimates are falling. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price is moving sideways. Resistance at 354.15–356.07 is close, and a typical daily move (ATR, the average daily range) is 7.66, so the gap to resistance is less than one ordinary day's move. The macro read is also negative. Enter only on a close above 356.07, or after a pullback that holds the 342.73–345.08 support zone.

decision.timing: Options price a 6.1% move by 2026-12-18 and an 11.1% move by 2027-02-19, which includes the 2027-01-28 report. That report is the next real test of inventory and growth, so there is no long-term buy above 300.56 before then.

change_mind: A drop to 300.56 or below, near the 200-day average of 302.08, would bring the price inside the value range and turn 'wait' into 'buy'.
If next-year profit-per-share estimates stop falling and climb back above the 10.84 level of 30 days ago, the growth case would get stronger.
If the 2027-01-28 report shows quarterly sales growth back near 16.6% with inventory under control, higher growth assumptions, toward the 387.1 value at 30% growth, would become more credible.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait on both horizons; the price now needs about 27.5% starting free-cash-flow growth (from about 27.6% yesterday), far above the 15% sales growth, which confirms the price is running ahead of value.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
